behavior_anomalies.why: The run begins with patients_requiring_ventilation at zero, but by t2 it already has four waiting patients and four patients on ventilators, with no preceding event creating patients requiring ventilation. The allocation therefore occurs without a causal transition from zero.
This increases hospitalized patients to 41 in a 40-bed hospital without any expansion, transfer, or overflow-capacity event.
Hospitalized patients rise to 45, exceeding the stated 40-bed capacity without a capacity change.

The synchronization reduces ventilators in use from five to four immediately after an allocation raised the patient and ventilator-use counts to five, with no patient recovery, extubation, or ventilator release event.

The synchronization again reduces ventilators in use from five to four without any corresponding clinical event releasing a ventilator, making the equipment-use state inconsistent with the allocation history.
The patient count starts at zero, but four ventilators are already recorded as in use before this allocation. The dependent in-use count should have been zero under the extreme condition.
When patients_on_ventilators reaches zero, ventilators.number_in_use remains 3 rather than falling to zero. Ventilators remain assigned without ventilated patients.
Hospitalized patients increase to 42 in a 40-bed hospital, exceeding the stated physical capacity without any overflow or expansion event.
Hospitalized patients again exceed the 40-bed capacity, reaching 47 without a stated cause or capacity expansion.

The log shows 7 patients requiring ventilation but only 3 on ventilators. With the waiting count initialized to zero, the expected consequence—no unmet patients—does not occur; at least four patients would have to be waiting or otherwise accounted for.
The hospital is defined as having 40 beds, yet this admission raises hospitalized patients to 41, exceeding physical bed capacity.
Hospitalized patients again exceed the fixed 40-bed capacity, reaching 46.
Hospitalized patients reach 52 in a 40-bed hospital, with no transfer, discharge, or capacity expansion shown.
Hospitalized patients reach 58, far beyond the hospital's 40 beds.

The stock synchronization increases ventilators in use to 4 even though the latest patient state shows only 1 patient on a ventilator: "t16 clinical-staff did release-one-ventilator: ... patients_on_ventilators 2->1 ... number_in_use 4->3". Ventilator use should track patients actually receiving ventilation, not increase without a corresponding patient assignment.
A 40-bed hospital cannot hospitalize 41 patients; this exceeds the stated bed capacity.
The hospital's ventilator capacity reaches 42, exceeding the hospital's 40 beds. Later dispatches increase it still further, making the equipment capacity physically inconsistent with the facility.
The scenario specifies a 40-bed hospital, yet hospitalized patients increase to 48, exceeding the hospital's physical bed capacity.

The hospital's ventilator capacity grows to 67 even though the scenario starts with only 6 ventilators and does not describe any physical expansion of the hospital. This is also inconsistent with the 40-bed facility.

After all patients are removed from ventilators, the ventilator stock still records 3 ventilators in use; the dependent resource count should be zero or otherwise match the number of patients on ventilators.
Allocating one ventilator to the only patient on a ventilator should make the number in use one, not five. The ventilator-use state changes independently of the patient count.
This raises hospitalized patients to 59 in a 40-bed hospital, with no bed expansion, discharge, or transfer event.
Ventilators in use increase from 3 to 4 during synchronization, without an allocation event; this is inconsistent with the preceding release event and with patients_on_ventilators remaining at 3.
Allocating one ventilator to raise patients_on_ventilators from 3 to 4 should raise number_in_use to 4, not 5; the two dependent quantities become inconsistent.
Synchronization removes one ventilator from use without a patient release event, while patients_on_ventilators remains 4.
Synchronization increases ventilators in use without an allocation event.
Synchronization decreases ventilators in use without a release event, while the preceding allocation left five patients on ventilators.
Synchronization increases ventilators in use without an allocation event.
The admission increases hospitalized patients by six while setting the available daily arrivals to zero. Under the zero-arrivals extreme condition, there should be no patients to admit.
Hospitalized patients continue increasing even though the hospital has only 40 beds; this raises occupancy to 54 without any overflow, diversion, or capacity consequence.

The ventilator stock reports an additional ventilator becoming in use without a corresponding patient allocation or increase in patients_on_ventilators. The logged patient state had previously reached zero ventilated patients.
The hospital is specified as having 40 beds, but this event increases hospitalized patients to 42.
Hospital occupancy continues increasing beyond the 40-bed capacity, reaching 48 patients.

The synchronization process reduces ventilators in use from 5 to 4 without any patient release or other freeing event immediately preceding it, while allocations continue to use the inconsistent lower count.

Supplier inventory repeatedly increases through replenishment with no production, delivery, or other source of the added ventilators/resources shown in the log, allowing the hospital's ventilator stock to grow to implausible levels.

The synchronization process increases ventilators in use from 3 to 4 without any allocation or other event putting a patient on a ventilator; it also increases the hospital's operational and owned stock to 89, exceeding the stated 40-bed hospital.
Ventilators in use increase from 3 to 4 without a corresponding allocation event. The same unsupported increase recurs during synchronization.
Ventilators in use again increase without a patient allocation or other cause.
Synchronization decreases ventilators in use from 5 to 4 even though no release event occurs at that time, making the resource state inconsistent with the preceding allocation.

Supplier inventory increases from 16 to 20 without a manufacturing, purchase, or other replenishment cause in the log. This unexplained replenishment repeats throughout the run, allowing inventory to grow despite dispatches.

The hospital's ventilator capacity reaches 59 and 55 ventilators are available, exceeding the stated 40-bed hospital capacity. The log shows no consequence such as rejecting, storing elsewhere, or otherwise limiting these deliveries.
This admits 41 hospitalized patients into a 40-bed hospital. The overflow continues later, including the transition from 40 to 46 patients, without any consequence such as refusal or transfer.

findings.finding: the conceptual model says 'occupied_beds' falls, but no rule ever decreases hospital.hospital_state.occupied_beds.
the conceptual model says 'occupied_beds' rises, but no rule ever increases hospital.hospital_state.occupied_beds.
the conceptual model says 'available_beds' falls, but no rule ever decreases hospital.hospital_state.available_beds.

rule replenish-medical-supplier-inventory creates supplier_stock.inventory from nothing; elsewhere that quantity only moves between things, so it must come from a stock that loses it.

with flu-patients patients_requiring_ventilation at zero: The run begins with patients_requiring_ventilation at zero, but by t2 it already has four waiting patients and four patients on ventilators, with no preceding event creating patients requiring ventilation. The allocation therefore occurs without a causal transition from zero. (run log: "t2 clinical-staff did allocate-one-available-ventilator: flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_on_ventilators 4->5; flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_waiting_for_ventilation 4->3; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_available 7->6; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 4->5") ALSO: This increases hospitalized patients to 41 in a 40-bed hospital without any expansion, transfer, or overflow-capacity event. (run log: "t7 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 35->41; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0") ALSO: Hospitalized patients rise to 45, exceeding the stated 40-bed capacity without a capacity change. (run log: "t19 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 39->45; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0")

with flu-patients patients_on_ventilators at zero: The patient count starts at zero, but four ventilators are already recorded as in use before this allocation. The dependent in-use count should have been zero under the extreme condition. (run log: "t2 clinical-staff did allocate-one-available-ventilator: flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_on_ventilators 0->1; flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_waiting_for_ventilation 4->3; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_available 7->6; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 4->5") ALSO: When patients_on_ventilators reaches zero, ventilators.number_in_use remains 3 rather than falling to zero. Ventilators remain assigned without ventilated patients. (run log: "t12 clinical-staff did release-one-ventilator: flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_on_ventilators 1->0; flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_requiring_ventilation 8->7; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_available 28->29; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 4->3") ALSO: Hospitalized patients increase to 42 in a 40-bed hospital, exceeding the stated physical capacity without any overflow or expansion event. (run log: "t18 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 36->42; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0")

with flu-patients patients_waiting_for_ventilation at zero: The log shows 7 patients requiring ventilation but only 3 on ventilators. With the waiting count initialized to zero, the expected consequence—no unmet patients—does not occur; at least four patients would have to be waiting or otherwise accounted for. (run log: "t3 clinical-staff did release-one-ventilator: flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_on_ventilators 4->3; flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_requiring_ventilation 8->7; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_available 8->9; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 4->3") ALSO: The hospital is defined as having 40 beds, yet this admission raises hospitalized patients to 41, exceeding physical bed capacity. (run log: "t7 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 35->41; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0") ALSO: Hospitalized patients again exceed the fixed 40-bed capacity, reaching 46. (run log: "t19 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 40->46; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0")

with ventilators number_available at zero: A 40-bed hospital cannot hospitalize 41 patients; this exceeds the stated bed capacity. (run log: "t28 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 35->41; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0") ALSO: The hospital's ventilator capacity reaches 42, exceeding the hospital's 40 beds. Later dispatches increase it still further, making the equipment capacity physically inconsistent with the facility. (run log: "t18 medical-supplier did dispatch-ventilators-to-hospital: hospital.hospital_state.ventilator_capacity 40->42; hospital.hospital_state.ventilators_available 36->38; medical-supplier.supplier_stock.inventory 58->56")

with medical-supplier inventory at zero: The scenario specifies a 40-bed hospital, yet hospitalized patients increase to 48, exceeding the hospital's physical bed capacity. (run log: "t28 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 42->48; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0") ALSO: The hospital's ventilator capacity grows to 67 even though the scenario starts with only 6 ventilators and does not describe any physical expansion of the hospital. This is also inconsistent with the 40-bed facility. (run log: "t30 medical-supplier did dispatch-ventilators-to-hospital: hospital.hospital_state.ventilator_capacity 66->67; hospital.hospital_state.ventilators_available 62->63; medical-supplier.supplier_stock.inventory 60->59") ALSO: After all patients are removed from ventilators, the ventilator stock still records 3 ventilators in use; the dependent resource count should be zero or otherwise match the number of patients on ventilators. (run log: "t19 clinical-staff did release-one-ventilator: flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_on_ventilators 1->0; flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_requiring_ventilation 4->3; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_available 38->39; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 4->3")

in an ordinary run: This raises hospitalized patients to 59 in a 40-bed hospital, with no bed expansion, discharge, or transfer event. (run log: "t26 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 53->59; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0") ALSO: Ventilators in use increase from 3 to 4 during synchronization, without an allocation event; this is inconsistent with the preceding release event and with patients_on_ventilators remaining at 3. (run log: "t4 process synchronize-hospital-ventilator-stock: ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 3->4; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_operational 16->17; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_owned 16->17") ALSO: Allocating one ventilator to raise patients_on_ventilators from 3 to 4 should raise number_in_use to 4, not 5; the two dependent quantities become inconsistent. (run log: "t9 clinical-staff did allocate-one-available-ventilator: flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_on_ventilators 3->4; flu-patients.flu_patients.patients_waiting_for_ventilation 4->3; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_available 21->20; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 4->5")

when 'admit-flu-patients' is repeated: The admission increases hospitalized patients by six while setting the available daily arrivals to zero. Under the zero-arrivals extreme condition, there should be no patients to admit. (run log: "t0 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 36->42; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0") ALSO: Hospitalized patients continue increasing even though the hospital has only 40 beds; this raises occupancy to 54 without any overflow, diversion, or capacity consequence. (run log: "t4 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 48->54; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0") ALSO: The ventilator stock reports an additional ventilator becoming in use without a corresponding patient allocation or increase in patients_on_ventilators. The logged patient state had previously reached zero ventilated patients. (run log: "t35 process synchronize-hospital-ventilator-stock: ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_available 74->77; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 3->4; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_operational 77->81; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_owned 77->81")

when 'allocate-ventilator' is repeated: The hospital is specified as having 40 beds, but this event increases hospitalized patients to 42. (run log: "t6 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 36->42; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0") ALSO: Hospital occupancy continues increasing beyond the 40-bed capacity, reaching 48 patients. (run log: "t15 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 42->48; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0") ALSO: The synchronization process reduces ventilators in use from 5 to 4 without any patient release or other freeing event immediately preceding it, while allocations continue to use the inconsistent lower count. (run log: "t2 process synchronize-hospital-ventilator-stock: ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_available 2->5; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 5->4; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_operational 7->9; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_owned 7->9")

when 'deliver-ventilators' is repeated: The synchronization process increases ventilators in use from 3 to 4 without any allocation or other event putting a patient on a ventilator; it also increases the hospital's operational and owned stock to 89, exceeding the stated 40-bed hospital. (run log: "t39 process synchronize-hospital-ventilator-stock: ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_available 82->85; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 3->4; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_operational 85->89; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_owned 85->89") ALSO: Ventilators in use increase from 3 to 4 without a corresponding allocation event. The same unsupported increase recurs during synchronization. (run log: "t21 process synchronize-hospital-ventilator-stock: ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 3->4; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_operational 50->51; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_owned 50->51") ALSO: Ventilators in use again increase without a patient allocation or other cause. (run log: "t22 process synchronize-hospital-ventilator-stock: ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_in_use 3->4; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_operational 51->52; ventilators.ventilator_stock.number_owned 51->52")

when 'order-ventilators' is repeated: Supplier inventory increases from 16 to 20 without a manufacturing, purchase, or other replenishment cause in the log. This unexplained replenishment repeats throughout the run, allowing inventory to grow despite dispatches. (run log: "t1 process replenish-medical-supplier-inventory: medical-supplier.supplier_stock.inventory 16->20")

when 'record-patient-status' is repeated: The hospital's ventilator capacity reaches 59 and 55 ventilators are available, exceeding the stated 40-bed hospital capacity. The log shows no consequence such as rejecting, storing elsewhere, or otherwise limiting these deliveries. (run log: "t39 medical-supplier did dispatch-ventilators-to-hospital: hospital.hospital_state.ventilator_capacity 58->59; hospital.hospital_state.ventilators_available 54->55; medical-supplier.supplier_stock.inventory 124->123")

when 'release-ventilator' is repeated: This admits 41 hospitalized patients into a 40-bed hospital. The overflow continues later, including the transition from 40 to 46 patients, without any consequence such as refusal or transfer. (run log: "t6 clinical-staff did admit-represented-flu-arrivals: flu-patients.flu_patients.hospitalized_patients 35->41; flu-patients.flu_patients.new_arrivals_per_day 6->0")
